contract.label: Scroll rail
contract.summary: A horizontal rail of `Card size="sm"` tiles that snaps and pages by whole tiles, carries the pill scrollbar in its foot, and bleeds 2px so no tile's ring is clipped by the scroll box.
contract.purpose: The horizontal rail of tiles — a fortnight of day tiles, a row of location cards — that snaps and pages by whole tiles. The rail carries the pill scrollbar (`scroll-rail`), bleeds 2px so the tiles' ring is never clipped by the scroll box, and gives the bar a foot of its own so it never overlaps the tiles' bottom edge.
useWhen: A card shows a sequence of equal tiles wider than the card — days, locations, items — and each tile is read whole.
The content pages sideways: the reader steps through tiles rather than skimming a cut-off edge.
dontUseWhen: The content is a vertical list or a table — that scrolls down in a `scroll-pane` or a `scroll-area`.
The tiles would be read as one strip rather than stepped through, or the whole set fits — then a `grid` of cards lays them out with no rail.

parts.name: ScrollRail
parts.description: The rail — a `ul` carrying the `scroll-rail` utility, `snap-x snap-mandatory`, the 2px bleed and the 6px foot the bar runs in. Give it a ref and page it with `scrollBy` from the host card's arrows.

parts.name: ScrollRailItem
parts.description: One stop — an `li` that snaps at its start edge and sets the tile's width; it holds a `Card size="sm"` at `h-full rounded-lg`.

requires: `Card size="sm"` at `h-full rounded-lg` inside every `ScrollRailItem`, and a width on the item (`w-44`, say) so the rail pages by it.

Paging arrows as `Button variant="outline" size="icon-sm"` with an `aria-label` and a `tooltip`, in the host card's `CardAction`, each shown only while tiles are off screen on its side (`useScrollRailEdges` on the rail, or an `IntersectionObserver` on the first and last tile at threshold 0.95).

The loading state is the same rail with a `skeleton` at each tile's shape; empty and error hold the rail invisible under a centred `text-body text-muted-foreground` message, so the card keeps its height.
forbids: A default OS scrollbar on the rail, or a hand-drawn 3px bar in page CSS — `scroll-rail` is the one scrollbar.
A hand-written bleed (`-m-0.5 p-0.5` on a plain `div`) or an `overflow-hidden` wrapper to hide the clipped ring — the rail already bleeds.
An edge fade on the rail: it pages by whole tiles, so the tile at its edge is a full one, and the fade would grey it out.
rules: A horizontal rail of tiles is `scroll-rail`: tiles are `Card size="sm"`, the rail snaps by tile, pages by whole tiles with no edge fade, carries the pill scrollbar, and bleeds 2px so the tiles' ring is never clipped.
The paging arrows live in the host card's `CardAction`, outline icon buttons with a tooltip, and each shows only while tiles are off screen on its side.
Past a threshold, a tile takes `bg-destructive-subtle ring-destructive/30` and its label `text-destructive-emphasis`; status is by meaning, never by position.
A vertical pane beside another is `scroll-pane`, not a rail.

behavior.loading: The same rail, with a `skeleton` at each tile's shape, so the card is already the height of the answer.
behavior.empty: The skeleton rail held invisible under a centred `text-body text-muted-foreground` message; the card keeps its height.
behavior.error: As empty, with the error's message; a retry, where there is one, is a `button` beside it.

requirements: The rail is a `ul`; give it an `aria-label` naming what it lists. Each tile is an `li`.
Each paging arrow carries an `aria-label` and a `tooltip`; the rail stays keyboard-scrollable without them.
The loading rail sits under `aria-busy` with a visually hidden sentence; the held message is a `role="status"` region.

examples: `<ScrollRail ref={setRail} aria-label="Daily forecast">{days.map((d) => <ScrollRailItem key={d.id} className="w-44"><Card size="sm" className="h-full rounded-lg">…</Card></ScrollRailItem>)}</ScrollRail>`
`const { canScrollBack, canScrollForward } = useScrollRailEdges(rail, days.length)` — then `rail.scrollBy({ left: rail.clientWidth })` from the forward arrow.
antiPatterns: A `flex overflow-x-auto` div of cards with the OS scrollbar showing under the tiles.
A rail whose edge tiles are faded with a mask, so the reader cannot tell a full day from a cut one.
Arrows that are always visible, or that sit beside the rail and shift the tiles when they appear.
